newsitem.title: CROATIA: Part of Croatia's biggest refinery modernised.
newsitem.headline: Part of Croatia's biggest refinery modernised.

text.p: The Croatian state oil company INA has modernised a plant for desulphurisation of diesel fuel at the country's biggest refinery in the Adriatic port of Rijeka, state radio said on Thursday.

"This investment totals 500 million kuna, but it will not be used only for the desulphurisation plant but also for maintenance work, to revamp the Rijeka refinery," head of the president's office Hrvoje Sarinic said on the radio.
The plant will enable the refinery to produce diesel fuel with 0.05 percent of sulphur, 20 percent less than before, to suit European ecological standards.
"This investment is an important energy saver and will contribute to safety at work and environment protection," Sarinic said.
"With this (plant), Croatia is becoming competitive in the world market," the radio quoted President Franjo Tudjman, who cut the ribbon to mark the end of the overhaul, as saying.
Sarinic said maintenance work, including replacing old equipment at two platforms, would be completed by June 30.
The works have been completed by INA-projekt of the INA group. The radio said it was the first major investment in the Rijeka refinery in the past 16 years. -- Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
